newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Chromecorp plant sees strike for higher pay.
newsitem.headline: Chromecorp plant sees strike for higher pay.

text.p: Chromecorp Holdings said on Thursday about 440 workers, more than half of them members of the National Union of Metalworkers (Numsa) of South Africa, had gone on strike at its Rustenburg Works Smelter over wages.
A spokesperson told Reuters production had not been affected as the plant was being manned by non-union members and that the plant was running at close to full capacity.
"Negotiations between union and the company reached an impasse on the issue surrounding entry level wages for the least skilled employees," the company said in a statement.
"Following the declaration of a dispute on the issue and the inability of the parties to achieve a mutually acceptable compromise, the union has elected...to engage in strike action," it said.
The company said it was pursuing "every conceivable avenue" in an attempt to normalise relations between itself, the union and the striking workforce.
The spokesperson said the smelter had the capacity to produce 280,000 tonnes of ferrochrome a year.
